AG126.question: To produce circular polarisation with Yagi-Uda antennas, a horizontal Yagi-Uda antenna and a second one rotated by 90 ° about the axis of radiation are connected together. What must be observed so that circular polarisation is actually produced?
AG126.answer_a: In one of the antennas, the wave must be delayed by $\lambda$/4. This can be achieved either by inserting an additional quarter-wave delay line or by mechanically "offsetting" the two Yagi-Uda antennas by $\lambda$/4 relative to each other.
AG126.answer_b: In one of the antennas, the wave must be delayed by $\lambda$/2. This can be achieved either by inserting an additional $\lambda$/2 delay line or by mechanically "offsetting" the two Yagi-Uda antennas by $\lambda$/2 relative to each other.
AG126.answer_c: The antennas must be connected together via a half-wave Lecher line. To match the characteristic impedance, a $\lambda$/4 transformer section must also be inserted between the feeder and the antennas.
AG126.answer_d: The crossed elements of the two antennas must be rotated by 45 ° so that they form a diagonal cross (X) in plan view. The antennas are connected in parallel via line sections of equal length. Matching is done with a balun.
